item.title: PHP2Shell CVEs Drive Criminal Forums Offline and Into Lockdown
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Oct 22:00 → 23 Oct 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

The adversary economy: How threat actors are reacting to PHP2Shell — Must Read

Following disclosure of the critical PHP2Shell RCE flaws, major criminal forums rapidly went offline or migrated infrastructure, underscoring that threat actors view vulnerable PHP systems as an existential risk. Organizations using PHP should urgently upgrade to supported versions or deploy compensating controls, as exploit commoditization is expected to follow quickly.

  • Two critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were publicly disclosed on October 20, 2026, and can be chained for more reliable exploitation.
  • Within 48 hours of the disclosure, criminal platforms including BreachForums, DarkForums, PwnForums, and Dread took measures such as going offline, restricting registrations, announcing maintenance, or moving communications to Telegram.
  • Criminal forum operators feared that the PHP flaws could expose member identities, private messages, financial records, IP logs, and stolen credentials to law enforcement or rival criminal groups.
  • All PHP versions below 8.3 are affected, while end-of-life branches including PHP 5.x, 7.x, 8.0, 8.1, and 8.2 will not receive patches and require migration to a supported version.
  • The article recommends that organizations unable to upgrade immediately deploy compensating measures such as web application firewalls, network segmentation, and enhanced monitoring for signs of exploitation.

Technologies: cms

Products: php, phpbb, tenable-one

Vendors: php, tenable, phpbb

item.title: Critical PHP2Shell and Node2Shell RCE Flaws Drive Urgent Patching
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Oct 18:00 → 22 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

PHP2Shell: One Upload, Full Server — Must Read

PHP2Shell comprises critical PHP flaws affecting versions back to 5.4 that can let unauthenticated attackers leak worker memory and potentially achieve remote code execution through crafted multipart uploads. Organizations should urgently inventory and patch PHP to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12, prioritize internet-facing systems, and rotate potentially exposed secrets.

  • PHP2Shell refers to two critical PHP CVEs, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that can allow unauthenticated attackers to read PHP worker memory and, in some cases, run code remotely.
  • The flaws affect PHP versions back to 5.4 across PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, and researchers demonstrated remote code execution against current WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla container images.
  • The disclosed attack chain uses a crafted multipart upload to trigger an out-of-memory error during PHP session upload-progress handling, leaving stale internal memory references in a reused worker.
  • Patched PHP releases are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, while PHP 8.1 and earlier have no official release.
  • Organizations are advised to inventory PHP installations, patch internet-facing systems first, investigate unusual multipart uploads and malformed PHPSESSID cookies, and rotate secrets on potentially exposed servers.

Technologies: web-server, cms

Products: php, php-fpm, opcache, apache-http-server, wordpress, drupal, joomla, frankenphp, litespeed, varonis-interceptor

Vendors: php, wiz, calif, varonis

Node2Shell: Node.js Brotli vulnerability allows remote code execution (CVE-2026-111497) — Should Read

Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497) is a high-severity Brotli decompression flaw that can enable crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution in vulnerable Node.js and Bun applications processing attacker-controlled compressed data. Upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1 or later, and Bun to 1.4.4 or later.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Node2Shell, is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that can be triggered by malformed compressed input and may cause crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution.
  • The affected Node.js release lines are fixed in versions 22.23.4, 24.22.1, and 26.12.1, while Bun is fixed in version 1.4.4 or later.
  • Applications can be exposed when they accept Brotli-compressed request bodies through Express 5 or body-parser 2.x, decompress untrusted data with node:zlib, or use fetch() to retrieve Brotli-compressed responses from outside servers.
  • Node.js 25.x, 23.x, 20.x, and earlier are end of life and will not receive a fix for this issue.
  • Rejecting inbound requests with Content-Encoding: br can reduce exposure temporarily, but only upgrading the runtime protects against Brotli-compressed responses fetched from other servers.

Vendors: nodejs-project, google, bun, expressjs, aikido, vercel

item.title: SEO Poisoning Campaign Delivers Armorsteal via Fake Chocolatey and Microsoft Activation Sites
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Oct 14:00 → 22 Oct 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

SEO Poisoning Campaign Delivers New Armorsteal Malware — Should Read

Zscaler identified an SEO poisoning campaign using fake Chocolatey and Microsoft Activation Scripts websites to distribute Armorsteal, a Python-based malware suite that provides remote access, keylogging, clipboard wallet hijacking, screenshots, and credential theft. Organizations should hunt for its scheduled tasks and files under C:\Windows\SystemHealth\Update\ and block the identified lure and C2 infrastructure.

  • Zscaler Threat Hunting identified an SEO poisoning campaign in September 2026 that used fake Chocolatey and Microsoft Activation Scripts websites to distribute the Python-based Armorsteal malware family.
  • The malicious installers requested elevated privileges, placed files in C:\Windows\SystemHealth\Update\, and created the SysCheck2 and SysCheckX scheduled tasks to launch Armorsteal at user logon and system boot.
  • Armorsteal’s remote access module collects system details, communicates with hardcoded command-and-control domains, and verifies RSA-2048 signatures before executing tasks received from its operators.
  • The surveillance module logs keystrokes, monitors and replaces cryptocurrency wallet addresses copied to the clipboard, captures keyword-triggered screenshots, and displays fake wallet transaction notifications.
  • The information-stealing module targets Discord tokens, browser cookies and saved passwords, cryptocurrency wallets and BIP39 seed phrases, password-manager data, SSH keys, and Steam session data.

Technologies: package-registry, antivirus, browser, remote-access

Products: chocolatey, microsoft-activation-scripts, python, pyarmor, microsoft-defender

item.title: Stadia RAT Emerges After StealC Takedown as eMudhra CA Keys Fail
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Oct 10:00 → 22 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

eMudhra CA compromise: eight private keys, and one of them is 4 — Should Read

eMudhra generated eight intermediate CA private keys with catastrophically weak values—one was simply 4—allowing attackers to forge certificates for arbitrary domains until clients block or remove the affected trust chains. Browsers have revoked them, but servers, containers, CLI tools, and bundled runtimes may remain vulnerable until their CA bundles and images are updated.

  • eMudhra generated eight intermediate certificate authority private keys incorrectly, and the article states that all eight are below 256, with one key equal to 4.
  • Anyone holding one of the compromised intermediate keys could sign a certificate for any domain, enabling impersonation for clients that still trust the affected certificate chains.
  • Firefox and Chrome blocked the certificates on October 17, 2026, while Apple blocked them on October 19 and Microsoft blocked them on October 20.
  • Command-line tools, containers, CI environments, and language runtimes may still trust the compromised intermediates because many do not check certificate revocation and may carry outdated certificate bundles.
  • The article advises updating operating systems and certificate bundles, rebuilding container images, restarting services, and testing whether clients reject the affected certificate chains.

Technologies: browser, operating-system, container-platform, ci-cd, iot-device

Products: emsign-ecc-root-ca-g3, firefox, chrome, ca-certificates, curl, git, openssl, certifi, docker, device-protection

Vendors: emudhra, mozilla, google, apple, microsoft, aikido, docker, debian, ubuntu, alpine-linux, fedora-project, python-software-foundation, openssl-project

StealC Is Back, and This Time It's a RAT — Should Read

The StealC operator has resurfaced after Operation Endgame with Stadia, a subscription-based RAT that retains StealC’s credential-stealing code while adding hidden remote desktop control, command execution, file management, process control, and in-memory loading. Defenders should hunt for its ProgramData-based persistence, hidden scheduled tasks, Defender exclusions, and HTTP POST C2 traffic carrying Base64-encoded RC4 ciphertext.

  • Europol’s Operation Endgame disrupted StealC in June by seizing 326 servers and 142 domains and recovering more than 25 million stolen credentials from 385,000 infected machines.
  • On October 16, the StealC seller resurfaced with Stadia, a subscription-based remote-access trojan that includes StealC-derived credential theft alongside hidden desktop control, remote command execution, file exploration, process management, and loading capabilities.
  • Varonis Threat Labs found that Stadia contains a 26,112-byte Chromium App-Bound Encryption helper that is byte-for-byte identical to a helper present in StealC 3.5 builds.
  • Stadia installs under a randomized 12-character directory in C:\ProgramData\, creates a hidden scheduled task that runs at logon and every 15 minutes, and may add a Microsoft Defender exclusion for its installation directory when elevated.
  • The analyzed Stadia build communicates over plain HTTP with hard-coded IP-address servers, sending RC4-encrypted and Base64-encoded data in HTTP POST bodies labeled as application/json.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, antivirus, browser

Products: stadia, stealc, windows, microsoft-defender, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, brave-browser

Vendors: varonis, microsoft, google, brave

A Norwegian Toll Bill Written From a Membership Template — May Read

A phishing email impersonated Norway’s AutoPASS toll system with a small 95 NOK payment demand, but reused a Danish membership-renewal template that exposed clear inconsistencies. Although SPF and DMARC passed, behavioral analysis flagged the malicious payment link and classified the message as phishing.

  • A role mailbox at a Norwegian IT consultancy received a payment reminder impersonating AutoPASS that requested 95 NOK, consisting of a 60 NOK toll charge and a 35 NOK late fee.
  • The email contained signs of a reused Danish membership template, including a Danish HTML language declaration, the Danish sign-off “Med venlig hilsen,” a “Medlemsservice” footer, and references to suspending a membership.
  • The message did not provide expected toll-bill details such as a vehicle registration, passage date, or toll station, despite referring to an invoice that was not shown.
  • The sender’s unrelated European domain passed SPF and DMARC checks, but the payment button linked to a path on an unrelated Portuguese company website that returned HTTP 404 during analysis.
  • Themis assigned the message 90% confidence and flagged its button link as malicious, resulting in automatic classification of the incident as phishing.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, ironscales-adaptive-ai

Vendors: ironscales

Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification — Optional

Cloudflare has obtained South Korea’s ISMS certification after a KISA-led audit, demonstrating that its security, privacy, and data-handling controls meet Korean regulatory requirements. To support compliance, Cloudflare implemented Korea-specific itemized consent during sign-up and disabled social sign-up paths that could bypass those required consents.

  • Cloudflare obtained South Korea’s ISMS certification under the ISMS-P framework following an audit by KISA-appointed auditors that reviewed 80 controls over ten days.
  • For South Korean sign-ups, Cloudflare presents separately labeled consent items, requires agreement to three required items before account creation, and makes marketing consent optional.
  • Cloudflare does not offer Google, Apple, or GitHub social sign-up in South Korea because those flows would bypass its required consent form.
  • The Korean sign-up experience is selected using the user’s chosen country and IP-based location, with the country selected by the user overriding the IP-based default.
  • The ISMS certificate is valid for three years and requires an annual audit to maintain it.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: cloudflare-workers, cloudflare-dashboard

Vendors: cloudflare, google, apple, github

How to contain shadow AI, as it takes on multiple forms and spreads throughout your environment — Optional

Shadow AI now includes local models, coding assistants, agents, MCP servers, browser extensions, and other unmanaged tools, creating major data leakage, compliance, and access-control risks. Organizations should pair employee education and clear, practical AI acceptable-use policies with continuous exposure management to discover, prioritize, and remediate unauthorized AI use.

  • Shadow AI has expanded beyond chatbots to include local models, coding assistants, autonomous agents, browser extensions, Model Context Protocol servers, APIs, and embedded AI features across enterprise environments.
  • IBM reported that 43% of organizations experienced security incidents involving shadow AI assets, and the average cost of a shadow AI-related data breach was $5.39 million.
  • Nearly half of shadow AI security incidents resulted in data loss or compromise, while 42% caused operational disruption and 21% triggered regulatory fines, according to IBM.
  • The article recommends educating employees and leaders about shadow AI, understanding why employees use unapproved tools, and creating an AI acceptable-use policy with approved tools and data-handling rules.
  • The article recommends treating shadow AI as part of broader exposure management by maintaining an inventory of AI assets, identifying security flaws and excessive permissions, prioritizing risks, and monitoring sensitive-data flows.

item.title: APT41 BlackX UEFI Bootkit Campaign and AI-Built Website Secret Exposures
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Oct 06:00 → 22 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia — Must Read

Kaspersky links a BlackLotus-like UEFI bootkit called BlackX to APT41, which targeted Central Asian diplomatic organizations after gaining administrator access and used it to disable defenses and deploy espionage payloads. Fully patched systems remained exposed because Microsoft’s Baton Drop mitigation requires administrators to manually activate Secure Boot certificate revocation.

  • Kaspersky identified an early-2026 campaign targeting diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan that used a UEFI bootkit named BlackX.
  • BlackX was installed after attackers compromised victim networks and obtained administrator privileges, and its installation chain closely resembled the BlackLotus use of the Baton Drop flaw to bypass Secure Boot.
  • The BlackX kernel driver attempted to tamper with security software, including security-related process, thread, and registry monitoring and event logging, while protecting bootkit files by returning handles to calc.exe instead.
  • BlackX delivered espionage payloads including a remote-access tool that used Google Drive, OneDrive, or Yandex.Disk for command-and-control communications and OxiDLLRunner, which contacted www.archivetj.com.
  • Kaspersky attributed the campaign to APT41 with medium confidence and found that targeted systems were fully patched but had not had Microsoft’s manual Secure Boot certificate-revocation step activated.

Technologies: operating-system, cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: windows, windows-boot-manager, secure-boot, google-drive, onedrive, yandex-disk

Vendors: microsoft, kaspersky, avast, google, yandex

The Keys Are in the Browser: Secret Exposure Across AI-Built Websites — May Read

Cyble found that 35 of 22,306 AI-built websites exposed live server-side credentials, including OpenAI, Stripe, Supabase, AWS, GitHub, and Slack keys, directly in public front-end code. Reused templates can spread a single exposed secret across many domains, enabling billing fraud, database compromise, cloud access, or internal phishing.

  • Cyble scanned more than 1.3 million newly registered domains and identified 22,306 websites built with AI app-builders.
  • Thirty-five of the identified AI-built sites exposed private credentials in public front-end code, including OpenAI API keys, Stripe secret keys, Supabase service-role tokens, AWS access keys, and GitHub or Google OAuth secrets.
  • Five sites exposed 16 OpenAI API keys, including one AI-writing site that shipped 12 distinct keys in its client-side bundle.
  • A shared Slack incoming-webhook URL appeared across 13 near-identical Bubble-hosted domains, while a single Stripe secret key was reused across four domains under two brands.
  • Cyble recommends keeping private keys in server-side functions or backend workflows, rotating any key that appeared on the client side, and reviewing shipped page code for exposed secrets.

Technologies: database, cloud-platform, source-control, identity-provider

Products: openai-api, stripe-api, supabase, slack-incoming-webhooks, aws, github, google-oauth, bubble, next-js, firebase

Vendors: cyble, openai, stripe, supabase, slack, amazon-web-services, github, google, bubble, vercel

  • The message did not provide a vehicle registration number, passage date, toll station, or the invoice it claimed had not been paid.
  • SPF and DMARC passed for an unrelated European sender domain, but those checks only confirmed that the domain’s server sent the email rather than that it represented AutoPASS.
  • The payment button led to a path on an unrelated Portuguese company website, and Themis flagged the link as malicious before automatically classifying the incident as phishing.

Detection engineering turns security telemetry into reliable, actionable alerts by balancing precision and recall through continuous testing, tuning, and measurement. item.title: PHP2Shell RCE Flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 Disclosed
item.content:encoded:

CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: PHP Vulnerable to Unauthenticated RCE Attacks — Must Read

Two critical PHP core flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (PHP2Shell), reportedly enable unauthenticated remote code execution on PHP 5.4+ systems. Organizations should urgently upgrade to patched supported releases or disable/isolate unpatchable PHP instances.

  • CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, were publicly disclosed on October 21, 2026 and are rated 9.2 out of 10 under CVSS v4.0.
  • The article states that all PHP versions from 5.4 onward are affected, while fixes are available for PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
  • The flaws can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute code on a vulnerable PHP server and potentially access sensitive memory containing passwords, tokens, API keys, or certificates.
  • The article describes CVE-2026-109618 as an out-of-memory error condition that can leave request data partially initialized, and CVE-2026-109619 as stale memory being accessed by a later request in the same PHP worker.
  • Organizations are advised to patch immediately, disable unpatched PHP services where possible, inventory PHP deployments, and isolate end-of-life instances that cannot yet be migrated.

item.title: PHP2Shell Emergency Patches and eMudhra Certificate Compromise Lead Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Oct 18:00 → 21 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

PHP2Shell: the fix is a runtime upgrade, not a code change — Must Read

PHP2Shell consists of two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws affecting PHP web runtimes; organizations should immediately inventory and upgrade all PHP deployments, including container base images, to patched releases or vendor-backported packages.

  • PHP released versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 on October 21, 2026, to address two critical remote code execution flaws collectively called PHP2Shell.
  • The flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, can allow an unauthenticated attacker to run code as the web worker account and potentially disclose memory from the worker process.
  • Every PHP installation serving web requests is affected, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, when running versions below the fixed releases.
  • Organizations should inventory PHP runtimes on hosts, virtual machines, container images, and hosting services, then upgrade to a fixed release or a distribution package that includes the patches.
  • Updating application code alone does not resolve the issue, and PHP advises restarting Apache, PHP-FPM, and long-running PHP workers after updating.

Technologies: web-server

Products: php, php-fpm

Vendors: php-project

Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates — Should Read

Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised by critically weak P-384 key generation, allowing attackers to forge trusted TLS or code-signing certificates. Organizations should apply vendor updates—particularly Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10—and verify that affected certificate chains are blocked across non-browser systems.

  • Eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised after a flawed April 30, 2025 key-generation process produced weak P-384 private keys with only 3 to 8 bits of entropy.
  • Six affected TLS intermediate certificates have been blocked by Chrome, Mozilla, and Apple, while two affected Microsoft code-signing certificates have also been blocked.
  • eMudhra revoked the compromised certificates and stopped issuing new certificates under its emSign Root TLS CA - G3 root.
  • The Go project released Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10 for CVE-2026-111943, filtering certificate chains containing the eight compromised eMudhra intermediate keys.
  • Cisco Talos had not observed malicious use of the compromised certificates in the wild as of October 21, 2026.

Technologies: browser

Inside a Global AI-Assisted Hacking Campaign — Should Read

Zscaler uncovered a globally targeted, financially motivated campaign in which a Chinese-speaking operator combined the ARTEX penetration-testing framework with AI coding assistants, multiple LLMs, and custom synchronization scripts to automate and persist offensive investigations. The activity sought personally identifiable information, transaction data, administrative access, and payment-related credentials across sectors including finance, dating, SMS, retail, cryptocurrency, and education.

  • Zscaler ThreatLabz reported that an operator combined the ARTEX penetration-testing framework with Claude Code, Codex, Grok, custom scripts, and configurations requesting DeepSeek, GLM, and Grok models.
  • The operator used work and jump servers, synchronization scripts, and saved project files to share instructions, preserve investigation context, and continue work across accounts and AI sessions.
  • Prompt histories from August through October 2026 showed targets in multiple industries and countries, including financial institutions, dating services, SMS providers, retail platforms, cryptocurrency services, educational services, logistics companies, and legal settlement systems.
  • The prompts included requests for personally identifiable information, phone numbers, transaction data, payment gateway API keys, administrative access, and methods to obtain NFT gifts without payment.
  • The recovered records indicated that the operator was Chinese-speaking and that the activity was likely financially motivated, based on requests to prepare stolen data for monetization and questions about selling compromised Korean data.

item.title: PHP2Shell RCE Exploitation and Compromised LiteLLM PyPI Release
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Oct 14:00 → 21 Oct 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Ships a Credential Stealer and Code Loader — Must Read

A malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 release on PyPI and associated container images installed Python startup hooks that stole extensive credentials and could fetch and execute remote code. Organizations that installed or ran this version—or affected latest tags—should remove the hooks without starting Python, rebuild from a known-clean pinned release, and rotate all accessible credentials.

  • A malicious LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was uploaded to PyPI on October 21, 2026, and PyPI stopped serving it in under two hours.
  • All seven malicious wheels installed cook.pth, cook.py, and sitecustomize.py into the root of site-packages, causing the payload to run whenever Python started.
  • The cook.py payload collected credentials and other sensitive data, including browser passwords, cloud credentials, SSH keys, CI secrets, AI-tool tokens, and LiteLLM proxy provider keys when DATABASE_URL was configured.
  • The sitecustomize.py payload launched a detached background process that checked a GitHub-hosted file hourly and could download and execute Python code from an attacker-selected host.
  • Malicious LiteLLM v1.107.0 Docker images were also distributed through Docker Hub and GHCR, including images served through latest, main-latest, and main-stable tags before removal.

Technologies: proxy, package-registry, container-platform, source-control, database

Products: litellm, pypi, github, docker-hub, github-container-registry, maturin

Vendors: berriai, python-software-foundation, github, docker

PHP Patches Critical RCE Vulnerabilities, Organizations Urged to Take Unpatched Sites Offline — Must Read

PHP released emergency patches for two critical PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution on web servers, with active attack traffic already observed. Organizations should upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 immediately, or isolate exposed applications until patching is complete.

  • PHP released emergency updates on October 21 for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two PHP2Shell flaws rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale that can enable unauthenticated code execution on web servers.
  • The fixed PHP releases are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, and administrators must update the PHP runtime serving web requests rather than only updating applications such as WordPress or plugins.
  • The NSA recommended taking affected systems offline until fully mitigated, while CERT-EU advised organizations unable to patch to consider isolating applications from public networks.
  • Cloudflare reported observing attack traffic and attackers modifying payloads to evade protections, while warning that its WAF rules are only a temporary stopgap.
  • W3Techs data cited in the article indicates that approximately 48.5% of PHP websites surveyed run branches that no longer receive routine PHP Project security updates.

Hunting Third-Party App Abuse in Entra — Optional

Compromised third-party Entra application credentials can let attackers access Microsoft 365 without user MFA, escalate privileges, and establish persistence by adding credentials to other apps. Hunt by correlating anomalous service-principal sign-ins with role or permission changes and secondary application credential creation.

  • Attackers used stolen ConnectWise application credentials to sign in to customer Microsoft 365 tenants as ConnectWise applications, and Huntress confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in at least 162 tenants.
  • Application-based sign-ins can bypass familiar user-focused indicators such as MFA prompts and interactive user sign-ins because no individual user account is used.
  • A compromised application with sufficient permissions can assign privileged directory roles, expand permissions, or add secrets and certificates to other applications for persistence.
  • Effective hunting should correlate unusual application authentication with privileged directory changes, credential creation on secondary applications, and continued access after containment.
  • Rotating or disabling the original compromised integration does not remove independent credentials that may have been added to other application identities.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, cloud-platform, backup

Your AI agent fixed the bug, but what else did it change? — Optional

Trail of Bits released patching-bugs and regression-hunt, agent plugins that standardize AI-assisted bug fixes and regression testing using live proof-of-concept evidence, defined schemas, and project-specific threat models. In preliminary tests, regression-hunt produced 25% fewer false positives than a baseline Codex PR review prompt, though some real regressions remained inconclusive.

  • Trail of Bits released the patching-bugs and regression-hunt plugins to help engineers delegate bug-fix development and regression checks to AI agents.
  • The patching-bugs plugin reproduces reported bugs, develops and tests fixes, uses a three-part proof involving original, patched, and reverted code, and requires regression-hunt analysis.
  • The regression-hunt plugin traces changed code to real interfaces, tests suspected regressions on running deployments, replays proofs with a fresh agent context, and judges whether the evidence meets its definition of a regression.
  • Trail of Bits reviewed more than 130 upstream-merged Patch the Planet pull requests and confirmed 21 regressions: 16 functional, one performance-related, and four involving builds or tests.
  • In preliminary evaluations using 21 confirmed regressions, regression-hunt generated 25% fewer false-positive findings than a Codex agent prompted to review a pull request for regressions, although some known regressions remained borderline due to insufficient evidence.
